proposals.description: This owner retains its original Difco/BD Marine Agar2216 dry-product denotation, supported by its creation history and the separately dosed powder in TOGO M2265. ATCC2887 lists a scratch preparation with17 dry ingredients and1000mL distilled water, whereas its separate product route uses55.1g BD212185 Marine Agar with1000mL water. The dry entries below retain the literal scratch-formula batch masses as source-qualified composition evidence; they are not a manufacturer lot analysis or a claim that the two routes have identical mass closure. Their sum is55.2520g, not the printed55.1g product dose. Both values are preserved without adjustment or an invented explanation (W04-CORRECTION-SOURCE-001; issue1233). Water remains explicit preparation context here, not a constituent of the dry product. Magnesium Chloride is printed without hydration; the previous CHEBI:86345 hexahydrate assertion is withdrawn and its source name/8.8g retained unresolved. Other inherited conventional salt identities are retained; no universal supplied-form purity claim is added.

It supplies no basal formula or vendor. DSMZ438 and ingredient2112 independently identify a Difco prepared basal medium with separate15% horse blood. These contexts establish the basal-versus-supplement boundary, but do not establish whether the two basal preparations have identical formulations or procurement identities. M2850 is not resolved to this Difco438 owner, no M2850 alias or recipe-equivalence is added, and the1L figure is the receiving recipe quantity, not an invented water component. The existing Difco438 identity and its partial component assertion remain unchanged. A source formula or product specification for M2850 that permits comparison with the Difco preparation is the remaining exact-identity fact.
